title: sessionless-bridge-auth-sanity-typed-errors-1.2.0
author: Marina Ortega
description:
Context: Cross-SDK parity work to reduce cognitive load for integrators and to harden streaming auth behavior that caused rare token handoff races in high-concurrency workloads. This PR implements a \"sessionless\" stream bridge for the Go SDK that decouples streaming client state from long-lived session objects, adds a typed error surface, harmonizes retry/backoff presets with TypeScript and Python, and bumps the Go SDK to v1.2.0. Motivation: Several production customers observed rare stalls during credential rotation when the stream consumer held onto a session object while a background reauth replaced tokens (race between send and rebind paths). The previous model also required the consumer to manage explicit session lifecycles, which is a common source of misuse across languages.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces sessionless.StreamBridge which maintains ephemeral per-stream credentials and performs in-line credential refresh with a single goroutine per bridge instead of per-session. This reduces goroutine proliferation and removes a hard-to-observe race where a session replace could outlive inflight requests.
- Adds a typed error package (errors/typed.go) that surfaces enumerated failure kinds (ErrTransient, ErrAuthExpired, ErrBackoffExceeded, ErrProtocolMismatch). Consumers can switch on concrete error kinds instead of string matching.
- Harmonizes retry presets with TS/Py: introduced RetryProfileLight, RetryProfileDefault and RetryProfileConservative and a lightweight adapter that maps SDK retry hints to the platform's centralized retry router. This aligns with ENG-1193/ENG-1195 and companion SDK PRs (TS: PR #670213, Py: PR #381207).
- UX/ergonomics: single-call consumer API StreamBridge.Start(ctx, opts) returns a typed iterator that supports ctx cancellation, .Pause()/.Resume() hints, and backpressure-friendly ReadFrame(ctx) semantics. The old SessionHandle API remains but is deprecated in favor of the sessionless flow.
- Version bump: updates go/sdk/version/version.go to 1.2.0 and a short migration guide in docs/upgrade/sessionless.md.

Commit summary (short):
- 9a1b3d: add sessionless StreamBridge implementation and core runtime loop
- d7c0f1: add typed error enums and conversion helpers
- f2e7aa: retry profile adapter and mapping table; add tests
- b3c9e5: add examples and migration docs
- 7f21d4: wire CI cross-checks and update changelog; bump version to v1.2.0

Files changed (high level):
- go/sdk/stream/bridge.go (new): core sessionless bridge loop and lifecycle
- go/sdk/stream/iterator.go (updated): typed iterator with context-aware ReadFrame
- go/sdk/auth/refresh.go (updated): inline refresh helper + jittered backoff
- go/sdk/errors/typed.go (new): typed error surface and constructors
- go/sdk/version/version.go (updated): bump to 1.2.0
- docs/upgrade/sessionless.md (new): migration steps and example
- examples/streaming/sessionless_example.go (new): end-to-end snippet
- tests/stream/sessionless_test.go (new): concurrency and rotation tests
- ci/integration/stream-check.yml (updated): run matrix across Go/TS/Py crosschecks
- python/sdk/sessionless_adapter.py (cherry-picked doc change): API note for migration (kept deliberately small to aid parity checks)

Testing and CI: All unit and integration suites were run in CI. Notable checks: go test (race) passed, integration-stream matrix passed against a local platform runtime fixture, TS and Py parity smoke checks ran in the job and passed. One intermittent flaky test (tests/stream/rebind_race_test) was quarantined and converted to deterministic harness; original flaky behavior reproduced locally prior to the fix which validated the change.

Review summary and conversation:
- Diego Marquez: \"This reduces goroutine churn and looks much cleaner. Concern: how does this interact with Dedicated slow-start? Please add a metrics hook for bridge_count and refresh_latency.\" (requested changes)
- Marina Ortega (author): \"Added bridge_count and refresh_latency histogram; pushed an extra commit to expose metrics via the Console shim.\" (resolved)
- Aisha Kapoor: \"Typed errors are very helpful — please ensure we keep conversion helpers for older consumers who still compare strings.\" (requested minor change)
- Marina Ortega: \"Added As() helpers and updated migration docs with examples using errors.Is/As.\" (resolved)
- Linus Park: \"Please add a migration note about deprecated SessionHandle and a short snippet showing equivalence.\" (approved after docs update)
- Final reviewers approved and CI green; PR was squash-merged to main on 2026-02-20.

Backwards compatibility and rollout guidance: The change is backwards-compatible but the SessionHandle API is deprecated (not removed). Recommend bumping application dependencies to v1.2.0 within a 2-week window for customers who previously managed session lifecycles. For high-throughput tenants, enable the new bridge behind an opt-in flag in Console; we plan to flip by default in 2 minor releases after additional telemetry collection.

Release notes: See release_notes field for structured bullets. Migration doc added at docs/upgrade/sessionless.md.

release_notes: SDK: Go SDK bumped to v1.2.0 — introduces sessionless StreamBridge (recommended) and deprecates SessionHandle.
UX: New typed errors (ErrTransient, ErrAuthExpired, ErrBackoffExceeded, ErrProtocolMismatch) for programmatic handling.
Reliability: inline credential refresh with single-goroutine bridge reduces goroutine pressure and fixes rare rebind races.
Interoperability: retry profile presets aligned across Go/TS/Py (RetryProfileLight/Default/Conservative).
notes_for_support: If a customer reports a regression after upgrading, ask for bridge_count and refresh_latency metrics and the output of 'go test -run TestSessionRotation -v' from their integration harness. For customers using SessionHandle heavily, recommend following the migration doc and lifting the opt-in flag if they have heavy token churn.
changelog: Added sessionless StreamBridge and typed errors; deprecated SessionHandle; bumped version to 1.2.0; migration guide added.
